answers.answer: Shuffle all 4 Conflict III cards and place them face down at the bottom; shuffle all 9 II cards and deal 5 above them; shuffle all 3 I cards and deal 1 on top. Return unused I and II cards to the box unseen.
answers.evidence: “Shuffle each entire tier before dealing”; “Return the unused I and II cards to the box unseen.”

answers.answer: In both games a human starts with 2 Agents on the Leader and a third (Swordmaster) beside the board; 3 troops in their garrison, 9 in supply, and 1 water. In a four-player game the Score marker starts at 1 VP; in a three-player game it starts at 0 VP. The Combat marker starts at 0 in either game.
answers.evidence: “Score track — on the 1 space in a 4-player game, otherwise on the 0 space”; “Take 1 water”; “three [troops] … remaining nine.”

answers.answer: Yes, you may take a Reveal turn while Agents remain, and after Revealing your turns are skipped for the rest of that phase, so you cannot later take an Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from cards revealed from your remaining hand, not cards played on Agent turns. At Clean Up, move all cards in front of you from both types of turns to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: “Agent turns are optional; you may take a Reveal turn while you still have Agents”; “Once you’ve taken a Reveal turn, your turns are skipped”; “Reveal box effects of the just-revealed cards only”; “Move all cards in front of you … to your discard pile.”

answers.answer: Resources gained only after Agent placement—from the destination or that played card’s Agent box—cannot pay that placement’s entry cost; pay before resolving either. On one card choose only one Agent icon and send one Agent. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used on an Agent turn; it can only be revealed.
answers.evidence: “cost immediately (before resolving any effects)”; “You choose only one Agent icon; one card can’t send multiple Agents”; “A card with no Agent icons … only … on a Reveal turn.”

answers.answer: At a Combat space, deploy all 3 troops recruited this turn plus up to 2 from the 4 already in your garrison, for a maximum of 5. At a non-Combat space, you do not deploy. Recruited troops come from your supply and are placed in your garrison until deployed.
answers.evidence: “any or all units recruited during your current turn … plus up to two more units from your garrison”; “recruits one troop: take it from your supply and place it in your garrison.”

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to any space connected to a post where you have a Spy, without recalling that Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy from a connected post to bypass another player’s Agent at that space; it cannot bypass your own Agent. Gather Intelligence recalls a Spy from a connected post to draw a card, chosen immediately after placing your Agent and before any space/card effects. You cannot use the same Spy for both; two different Spies can pay for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence on one placement.
answers.evidence: “Spy Agent icon … do not recall”; “Infiltrate … ignore the other player’s Agent”; “Gather Intelligence … immediately after placing”; “cannot recall the same Spy to both.”

answers.answer: Strength is 11: 2 troops = 4, one sandworm = 3, and four swords = 4. If your last unit is removed, your strength becomes 0. With no unit in the Conflict, you cannot participate in the Combat Intrigue window.
answers.evidence: “Each troop … 2 strength; each sandworm … 3; each sword … 1”; “if your last unit is ever removed, your strength becomes 0”; Combat Intrigue for players with “at least one unit.”

answers.answer: Yes. Passing does not prevent you acting again after another player plays; the window closes after all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not garrison), sandworms return to the bank.
answers.evidence: “not required to pass just because you passed earlier”; “Once all players involved … pass consecutively”; “troops … to their supply”; “sandworms return to the bank.”

answers.answer: If exactly two players tie for first in a four-player game, each receives the second reward; the remaining players compete for the third reward. Nobody wins the Conflict or takes its card. In a three-player game, the two tied players each receive the second reward and there are no other rewards. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.
answers.evidence: “exactly two tied for first [in four players] … remaining players compete for the third”; “nobody takes the card”; “with three or fewer players no other rewards”; “0 strength receives no reward.”

answers.answer: One or more sandworms double your rewards once; multiple worms do not quadruple. Taking control and battle icons on a won Conflict card cannot be doubled. For a reward allowing 3 spice for 1 VP, you may pay the 3-spice cost again to take that reward a second time, for 2 VP total at 6 spice total; the optional second payment is permitted because the reward is doubled.
answers.evidence: “one or more sandworms … double”; “control … nor … battle icons”; “may pay the cost a second time … or 6 spice to gain 2.”

answers.answer: After winning, take the Conflict card face up into your supply, then check it for a matching face-up Conflict or Objective card; a matching pair must be flipped face down for 1 VP. In Endgame, a wild icon may match any one of the three icons in your supply, flipping the pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: “Take the won Conflict card face up … Then check … mandatory matching pair”; “face-up Conflict or Objective”; “During the Endgame … wild … any one.”

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP and lose that VP if you fall below 2; regain it on reaching 2 again. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained below 4 and earned again on returning to 4. First to 4 also takes the Alliance and its 1 VP; that VP follows the token. Merely tying the holder does not take the Alliance: you must rise above them (or the separate FAQ holder-loss trigger can transfer it).
answers.evidence: “At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; lose it below 2”; track bonus “keep it if you fall below 4”; “tying … does not steal the Alliance.”

answers.answer: During Reveal, Persuasion may be spent before, between, or after Reveal effects. Pool it across sources to buy one card or split one source among cards; acquire as many as affordable, with unused Persuasion lost at the end of Reveal. The Imperium Row is replenished to five immediately, so you can buy a replacement in the same Reveal if affordable. Put acquired cards face up in your discard pile.
answers.evidence: “before, between, or after”; “pool … or split”; “Row must always have five cards”; “face up into your discard pile”; “never be saved.”

answers.answer: At each Maker space left without an Agent in Makers, add 1 spice to its bonus spot; a visitor gains all accumulated bonus spice. Maker Hooks are required only when the particular summoning effect specifies them; Hooks are retained, not spent. The Shield Wall blocks summoning to Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, and Imperial Basin while it remains. Sandworms are placed directly in your Conflict quadrant, never in a garrison; once the Wall is removed, any Conflict may receive them.
answers.evidence: “place 1 spice … adds to any bonus spice”; visitor gains “all”; “Hooks are not a universal prerequisite”; “Shield Wall … no sandworm”; “never … garrison.”

answers.answer: The game-end condition is checked at Recall, at the end of a round: 10 or more VP by any player or an empty Conflict Deck triggers Endgame. Players first play and resolve any Endgame Intrigues, then compare total VP. Rulebook tiebreakers, in order, are spice, Solari, water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: “At the end of a round … Endgame is triggered”; “First, players may play … Endgame Intrigue”; tiebreakers “spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops.”

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM setup has 2 contracts face up and 18 face down in the bank when Shaddam is not chosen. Shuffle in 4 additional Intrigue and 4 additional Imperium cards. Shaddam is optional. The 10 contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts stay in the box and are not part of the 20 standard contracts.
answers.evidence: “With no Shaddam … two offers and 18 in the bank”; “Shuffle the 4 additional…”; “A player may choose … optional”; contrasting set “leave them in the box.”

answers.answer: With CHOAM and available contracts, the icon takes one face-up contract and replaces it from the bank face up; without CHOAM, or when all contracts have been taken, it gives 2 Solari. A Harvest contract completes by sending an Agent to a Maker space and gaining at least its shown spice amount that turn in total; Immediate completes upon taking it; Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: contract icon “take one … then replace”; “reverts to giving 2 Solari”; Harvest… “amount of spice shown during that turn (in total)”; “Immediate … as soon as you take it”; acquire contract “when you next acquire.”

answers.answer: No. You must have held a board-space contract when you sent the Agent, so one taken after visiting that space waits until a future turn. On completion, announce it, gain its shown rewards, then flip it face down and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: “must wait until a future turn … must have had the contract at the time”; “announce it, gain the rewards … flip it face down and leave it in your supply.”

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor. The Rival gets the Ornithopter Objective; the humans receive the other two eligible Objectives, and the human whose card shows First Player takes the marker. First Player alternates only between the humans; order begins First Player → Rival → other human. The Rival takes Agent turns but never Reveals.
answers.evidence: “one shared scoring Rival”; “Give the Rival the Ornithopter Objective”; “First Player alternates only between humans”; “First Player → Rival → other human”; “Rival never Reveals.”

answers.answer: For an occupied indicated destination, ignore it and reveal another Hagal card. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: try an empty post of the specified type, ignore placement if none exists, then reveal another card either way. Ignore normal space costs/effects and apply only Hagal effects. If the deck empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
answers.evidence: “Ignore an occupied destination and reveal again”; Place Spy: “immediately reveal another Hagal card”; “Ignore normal space costs and effects”; “reshuffle … and continue.”

answers.answer: For 3–4 players, omit Objectives marked for the wrong player count, shuffle eligible cards, and deal one face up to each player; the card marked with the First Player marker determines first player. Shaddam may be used only with the CHOAM Module, so not in a game without it.
answers.evidence: “omitting any whose … marking doesn’t match”; “one random Objective face up”; “Do not use Shaddam … unless playing with the CHOAM Module.”

answers.answer: The resource and sandworm supplies are not limited; substitute conveniently if the bank runs out. By contrast, if your personal troop supply is empty, you cannot recruit until troops return to it. Payments of Solari, spice, or water return to the bank.
answers.evidence: “not meant to be limited — make any convenient substitution”; “can’t recruit more until some return”; “whenever you pay … return it to the bank.”

answers.answer: The five phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal the Conflict first, resolve any controlled-location defensive troop, then each player draws five. If Endgame is not triggered at Recall, humans return Agents to their Leaders; First Player passes clockwise in 3–4 human games, while in two-player play Rival Agents return to supply and First Player passes to the other human.
answers.evidence: Five-phase order and Round Start sequence; Recall instructions in “prepare the next round.”

answers.answer: Yes: resolve space effects, Agent-box effects, and the Faction advance in any order. No: the visit’s Influence cannot meet that space’s entry requirement, because costs and requirements must be met before placement/effects.
answers.evidence: “You may carry out all these effects in any order”; “must pay any costs and meet any requirements” before gaining effects.

answers.answer: No, an optional arrow cost/effect can be paid and taken only once per turn, even if you have more resources. Most card and space effects are mandatory; “may,” optional arrow costs, and the black-X trash icon are optional, while direct instructions (including a card’s own trash instruction) are mandatory. Intrigue conditions and costs must be met to play it.
answers.evidence: “pay the cost and gain the effect only once per turn”; FAQ “Most … mandatory. Exceptions include ‘may,’ arrow costs …”; “Intrigue conditions and costs must be met.”

answers.answer: A Spy placement icon places a Spy from supply on an unoccupied observation post. If you have none in supply, you may first recall one of your Spies for no effect. When the placement effect specifies a required Agent-icon type, the connected post must meet it or placement is impossible.
answers.evidence: “unoccupied observation post”; “if … no Spies … may first recall one … for no effect”; specified icon “must be connected.”

answers.answer: Infiltrate cannot bypass your own Agent. You may recall a Spy without that recall being printed on a card to Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence, but an Agent turn still requires playing a card. You cannot use two Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on one placement; you may use one for Infiltrate and a different one for Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: “A Spy may also be recalled without a card”; FAQ: recall still requires a card for the Agent turn; “never two to Gather Intelligence on the same placement.”

answers.answer: When anyone visits a controlled critical location, its controller gains the separate location bonus: 1 Solari at Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, 1 spice at Imperial Basin; this can be the visitor too. Winning that location’s Conflict places/replaces its Control marker. When its Conflict is revealed, the controller may deploy one troop from their supply without an Agent visit.
answers.evidence: “whenever any player … sends an Agent there”; “Winning … includes control”; “may deploy one troop from your supply.”

answers.answer: In a three-player tie for second, each tied player gets the third reward; the first-place winner keeps first reward and the card, with no further rewards. A tie for third gets nothing. If three tie for first, each gets the second reward and nobody takes the Conflict card; no other rewards are given, including to a remaining fourth player.
answers.evidence: Tie rules table: “Second … each … third reward”; “Third … nothing”; three tied first: “Each gets the second reward; nobody wins or takes … no other rewards.”

answers.answer: With three different positive strengths, first and second place receive their printed rewards; third receives none. This is also true in a two-human game with the Rival as the third competitor: ordinary first and second receive rewards, and ordinary third does not.
answers.evidence: “with 2 or 3 players (including two humans plus a Rival), ordinary first and second place receive rewards”; third “receives nothing.”

answers.answer: Plot Intrigues may be played during your own Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigues only during Combat and with at least one unit deployed; Endgame Intrigues at game end. Keep Intrigues face down, separate from your deck, until played; after resolving, put them face up in an Intrigue discard pile. If the Intrigue Deck runs out, shuffle its discard to form a new deck.
answers.evidence: Intrigue timing and storage in Special Rules; FAQ: “If the Intrigue deck runs out, shuffle its discard…”

answers.answer: An ordinary discard instruction discards a chosen card from your hand and cannot discard an Intrigue unless specified. The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon lets you trash one Intrigue of your choice from hand. Secrets steals one Intrigue chosen at random from each opponent who has at least four.
answers.evidence: “discard a card … from your hand”; “cannot be an Intrigue … unless specified”; “trashes one Intrigue of your choice”; Secrets “four or more … selected at random.”

answers.answer: A trash effect can remove cards from your hand, discard pile, or in play. Return ordinary trashed cards to the box; Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless paying a cost or directed to trash itself. Trashing The Spice Must Flow does not remove the VP already gained on acquisition.
answers.evidence: Trashing section; FAQ: “The Spice Must Flow’s acquire VP is retained if the card is later trashed.”

answers.answer: Acquire-box effects resolve once when you acquire the card. When you cannot draw because your deck is empty, reshuffle your discard pile into a new deck and keep drawing. Unused Persuasion is lost at the end of your Reveal turn, not carried over.
answers.evidence: “gain that effect one time, at the moment you acquire”; reshuffle when deck empty; Persuasion “never be saved.”

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and revealed during Reveal remain face up in play until Clean Up, unless trashed first. Fremen Bond can use one or more other Fremen cards in play; two Bond cards can activate each other regardless of play order. They cease being in play at Clean Up.
answers.evidence: “remain face up and ‘in play’ until you Clean Up”; “two Fremen Bond cards can activate one another.”

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the one just placed; you can use that returned Agent on a later Agent turn in the same round. Retreat sends a troop from the Conflict to your garrison. ‘Retreat any number’ allows zero.
answers.evidence: “Return one of your other Agents”; “may use it again on another Agent turn”; “Retreat … back to your garrison”; FAQ “allows zero.”

answers.answer: A free-choice effect granting two Influence requires both advances to go to one chosen Faction; it cannot be split. An Alliance icon requires you to hold that Faction’s Alliance token; a minimum-Influence effect requires the stated Influence level.
answers.evidence: “when gaining two, you can’t choose two different Factions”; Alliance icon “requires you to hold”; card effects “require a minimum Influence.”

answers.answer: If the holder loses Influence after being tied with two opponents, the holder chooses which formerly tied opponent receives the Alliance. If the holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4+, return the token to the board; the former holder loses its VP.
answers.evidence: FAQ: “if several were tied, the former holder chooses its recipient”; if “nobody has 4+ … return the token”; “old holder loses 1 VP.”

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used that turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round and added on top of the usual five cards. A Plot Intrigue with a later Reveal effect stays face up until Reveal, is used then, and is discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ “Drawn during Reveal means immediately reveal and use”; after Reveal “keep it for next round”; Plot “stays face up until then.”

answers.answer: No. A ‘when you win’ Intrigue cannot be played after tying for first because nobody wins. If you receive that Intrigue as a reward for an outright win, you may play it immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ: “‘When you win a Conflict’ Intrigues cannot be played after tying for first”; “if received as a winning reward they can be played immediately.”

answers.answer: If VP and all four resource tiebreakers are still tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed 12.
answers.evidence: FAQ: “If all four resource tiebreakers remain tied … most recently took a Reveal turn wins”; “Scores may exceed … 12.”

answers.answer: Yes, all contracts held for the same space must be fulfilled with one Agent placement; you cannot defer them after that visit. Contract effects are another effect of that Agent turn and can resolve in any order with the space and Agent-box effects, provided you held the contract when placing the Agent.
answers.evidence: FAQ: “Fulfill all contracts you hold for the same space with one Agent placement”; “can resolve in any order”; must hold it when sending.

answers.answer: Shaddam does not start with the two set-aside Sardaukar contracts. Only Shaddam may choose one when he acquires a contract, in place of a generally available one. His Signet Ring deployment restriction applies immediately when Signet Ring sends the Agent and lasts for that turn only, not the whole round.
answers.evidence: “reserved for his exclusive acquisition but do not begin in his possession”; FAQ: “only Shaddam”; “takes effect immediately … lasts only for that turn.”

answers.answer: Feyd starts with his token on the leftmost Training-track space and leaves it on the rightmost space once reached. Lady Jessica starts with her Lady Jessica side face up, not Reverend Mother Jessica. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: Feyd “leftmost … remains [rightmost]”; “Lady Jessica side face up”; FAQ “may use her ability on the turn she flips.”

answers.answer: Moving from 1 to 3 Influence counts as reaching 2. You can reach 2 with the same Faction again after losing Influence and later moving up; moving down through 2 does not count. Moving Guild’s Favor from play to discard during Clean Up does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from your hand does.
answers.evidence: Margot/Irulan “reach 2 … moving past 2”; “only … moving up”; Guild’s Favor Clean Up “does not trigger.”

answers.answer: Accept Contract uses Spice Trade, has no cost, is not a Combat space, always draws one card, and gives the contract-icon effect (2 Solari without CHOAM or when contracts are exhausted; otherwise take and replace a contract). It gives no automatic Faction Influence. Dutiful Service uses Emperor, has no cost, is not Combat, gives one Emperor Influence and the same contract-icon effect; it advances Emperor once total, not twice.
answers.evidence: Board table and shared rule: Accept Contract Spice Trade, Dutiful Service Emperor; “Always draw one card”; “Dutiful Service … gain 1 Emperor Influence, counted once”; contract icon rule.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City access, no cost, Combat yes; visitor recruits one troop and draws one card, while its controller gains 1 Solari. Fremkit: Fremen access, no cost, Combat yes; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw a card. Research Station: City access, costs 2 water, Combat yes; recruit two troops and draw two cards.
answers.evidence: Board space table rows Arrakeen, Fremkit, Research Station.

answers.answer: Deep Desert costs 3 water; choose 4 base spice or, with Hooks, summon two worms. Hagga Basin costs 1 water; choose 2 base spice or, with Hooks, summon one worm. Both give all accumulated bonus spice regardless of choice. Hooks are retained, not spent. These are Combat spaces.
answers.evidence: Board table Deep Desert/Hagga; Sandworm rule: “Hooks … never spent”; Maker space says “gain all bonus spice.”

answers.answer: Both options require City access and 2+ Fremen Influence and have no resource entry cost. Option one takes Maker Hooks if you lack them, recruits one troop, and gains 1 water. Option two gains 1 water and optionally removes the Shield Wall; it does not recruit a troop.
answers.evidence: Sietch Tabr row lists options; heading confirms both access/requirement; no troop in second option.

answers.answer: High Council uses Landsraad, is not Combat, and costs 5 Solari each visit. First visit places your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and grants 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. Later visits give 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, and recruit three troops.
answers.evidence: High Council row in board table.

answers.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone obtains it and 6 Solari once anyone has one; each player may visit only once per game. Take the third Agent from beside the board onto your Leader; it is available this round and for the rest of the game. A Rival obtaining its Swordmaster also lowers the human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Swordmaster row in board table.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege uses Landsraad, is not Combat, costs 3 Solari and requires 2+ Emperor Influence. You may discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue; recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It gives no automatic Emperor Influence.
answers.evidence: Imperial Privilege row; only Faction spaces give automatic advance and it is Landsraad.

answers.answer: Shipping uses Spice Trade, is not Combat, costs 3 spice and requires 2+ Spacing Guild Influence. It gives 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction, which need not be the Guild.
answers.evidence: Shipping row: “1 Influence with any one Faction”; not a Faction space.

answers.answer: Gather Support is Landsraad and not Combat: choose to pay 0 or 2 Solari; recruit two troops, and if you paid 2, also gain 1 water. Spice Refinery is City and Combat: choose to pay 0 or 1 spice; gain 2 Solari, or 4 Solari if paying 1 spice; controller gains 1 Solari in either case.
answers.evidence: Board table Gather Support and Spice Refinery rows.

answers.answer: Heighliner: 5 spice, +1 Guild Influence, recruit 5 troops, Combat yes. Desert Tactics: 1 water, +1 Fremen Influence, recruit 1 troop, optionally trash a card, Combat yes. Sardaukar: 4 spice, +1 Emperor Influence, draw an Intrigue, recruit 4 troops, Combat no.
answers.evidence: Board table rows Heighliner, Desert Tactics, Sardaukar.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall is Landsraad, no cost, not Combat; draw an Intrigue and gain 1 Persuasion during Reveal if your Agent is there. Espionage is Bene Gesserit, costs 1 spice, not Combat; gain 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draw a card, place a Spy. Deliver Supplies is Spacing Guild, no cost, not Combat; gain 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Board table rows Assembly Hall, Espionage, Deliver Supplies.

answers.answer: False Orders moves each affected opponent’s Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent’s destination that turn; it may be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear’s red box is ignored during Reveal, or when it gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ False Orders and Litany rulings.

answers.answer: Manipulate prevents opponents from acquiring the removed card. You may acquire it by another means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If still unacquired at the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ: “opponents cannot acquire”; “without the 1-Persuasion discount”; “end of your next Reveal, remove it from game.”

answers.answer: The Rival starts with four Influence cubes at track bottoms, three troops in garrison and the rest in supply, two Agents in supply with Swordmaster beside the board, three Spies and 1 water; its score and Combat markers start at 0. Shuffle House Hagal and retain the 2P Reshuffle card. If it reaches 10 VP, Endgame triggers at Recall and it can win.
answers.evidence: Rival Setup paragraph and “its 10+ VP triggers Endgame at Recall just like a human’s score.”

answers.answer: The Rival counts Solari, spice, Intrigue cards, and water together, each unit/card counting as one; when the total reaches its printed Swordmaster threshold, it spends that many. Spend Solari first, then spice, then Intrigue cards, then water; keep leftovers. Its third Agent is usable in the current round.
answers.evidence: “Count Solari, spice, Intrigue cards and water together, each unit counting as one”; threshold, spend order, leftovers, current-round availability.”

answers.answer: After Swordmaster, the Rival spends each set of 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water for 1 VP. A mixed total of seven resources is not one of those sets and earns no VP.
answers.evidence: “whenever it has 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water, spend each such set for 1 VP.”

answers.answer: The Rival chooses the Faction with least Influence, breaking ties by leftmost priority icon. It receives VP at 2 Influence and the Alliance VP when it holds the Alliance, like a human; it does not receive the resource bonus for reaching 4. A numbered Hagal Influence icon refers to that position in its Faction priority list.
answers.evidence: Rival combat/influence rules and “numbered Influence icon refers to that position”; “gains and loses Influence VP and Alliances like a human, but does not receive resource bonus.”

answers.answer: No. For a two-destination Hagal card, use only the destination whose condition applies (Guild Influence for Accept Contract/Shipping; Conflict tier for Deliver Supplies/Heighliner). If that selected destination is occupied, reveal another Hagal card; do not use the other destination.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns paragraph.

answers.answer: Yes. At every Combat space the Rival deploys up to two available garrison troops even if that Hagal card recruited none. Newly recruited troops at a noncombat space go to garrison. A conditional 2+ Influence bonus is ignored if unmet, but its absence does not prevent placing the Agent.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: “at a Combat space also deploy up to two”; “otherwise put [recruits] in garrison”; “lack of that bonus never prevents placing.”

answers.answer: Unless a post type is specified, the Rival places a Spy at the first available Faction observation post in its priority order; if all four are occupied, ignore placement. Placing its third and final supply Spy recalls its other two Spies and triggers its Scheme. It never recalls Spies for Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes paragraph.

answers.answer: If its Scheme recruits troops before a Combat-space placement that same turn, those troops are deployed too. A Place Spy card with no legal post is ignored, then the Rival reveals another Hagal card because no Agent was sent.
answers.evidence: “If a Scheme recruits troops before Agent placement … deploy those troops too”; Place Spy rule.

answers.answer: At Hagga Basin/Deep Desert the Rival always collects all bonus spice. With Hooks and a Conflict permitting worms, it summons one/two worms instead of base spice. If it summons none—because it lacks Hooks or the Conflict is protected—it takes base spice (Hagga 2, Deep Desert 4).
answers.evidence: Rival Maker spaces paragraph.

answers.answer: At Combat start, if the Rival has at least one deployed unit, reveal a Hagal card in turn order and add its bottom swords to its strength; if Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. This happens before humans’ normal Combat Intrigue window, so humans may respond afterward. A Rival with no deployed unit gets no bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat paragraph: beginning of Combat, if unit; reveal; “Humans then have their normal … window.”

answers.answer: Yes: the Rival gets control bonuses on visits and the defensive troop when its Conflict is revealed; it wins Conflict cards and battle-icon VP and doubles rewards with worms. It always takes an optional Conflict VP if it can pay resources or recall required Spies. A contract reward gives it 2 Solari, even with CHOAM; it never takes contracts.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat paragraph.

answers.answer: During Reveal effects, total and announce Combat strength and set the marker at any point; update it as needed while resolving the turn. Strength over 20 is marked by flipping to the +20 side and starting again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn “at any point while resolving, updating as needed”; Strength section on +20 marker.

answers.answer: A Leader’s Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on one of your Agent turns, not when you merely reveal it. Cards of any type can override the usual game rules.
answers.evidence: Setup Leader rule and Overview: “Cards of any type can override the usual rules.”

answers.answer: A Recall Spy icon on a card returns one of your Spies from a post to your supply, usually as the card’s cost for a powerful effect. It does not itself mean Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those are separate optional recalls without a card.
answers.evidence: “Recall Spy icon … returns … to your supply”; separate Spy recalls for Infiltrate/Gather Intelligence.

answers.answer: The trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. An ordinary discard instruction discards a chosen non-Intrigue card from your hand, unless it specifically says otherwise.
answers.evidence: “separate trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand”; “Discarding” rule.

answers.answer: When a single Influence reward is doubled, its two instances may go to the same Faction or to two different Factions. In contrast, one effect granting two freely chosen Influence must put both in one Faction.
answers.evidence: Sandworm reward example: “same Faction or two different Factions”; Influence rule “when gaining two, you can’t choose two different Factions.”

answers.answer: Resolve the Signet Ring ability printed on the Rival card, not its Scheme. The Hagal Signet icon itself triggers it; no human Signet Ring card or Rival Reveal turn is involved.
answers.evidence: Rival Signet Ring and Scheme table.

answers.answer: A Hooks icon gives the Rival one token only if it lacks one; if it already has one, it takes no additional token. Shield Wall removal works only if the Rival has Hooks and the Wall remains. Without Hooks it is ignored; if the Wall is gone, there is no further effect.
answers.evidence: Rival Hooks and Wall icons table.

answers.answer: Secrets uses Bene Gesserit, has no cost and is not Combat. It grants 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draws an Intrigue from the Intrigue Deck, and takes one Intrigue chosen at random from each opponent with 4 or more Intrigues.
answers.evidence: Secrets row and Special Rules steal rule.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin uses Spice Trade, has no entry cost, and is a Combat space. The visitor gains 1 base spice plus all bonus spice; if the visitor controls it, they separately receive the controller’s 1 spice bonus too (2 base total plus bonus).
answers.evidence: Imperial Basin row: “Gain 1 base spice plus all bonus spice; controller gains 1 spice”; controlled location rules.

answers.answer: At Round Start, reveal the top Conflict and place it face up next to the deck, on top of any unclaimed cards from earlier rounds. Then resolve the defensive troop bonus, then each player draws five cards. So Conflict is revealed before drawing hands.
answers.evidence: Round Start: “place it face up … on top of any Conflict cards remaining from previous rounds”; “Then each player draws five.”

answers.answer: Each player starts with one cube on the bottom of each of the four Faction Influence tracks. The four Alliance tokens begin on their respective tracks, so no player begins holding one. The Shield Wall token starts on its marked space below Spice Refinery.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 6: Alliance tokens placed on tracks; “Place four cubes … on the bottom”; Shield Wall on marked area.

answers.answer: In 3–4 player play, the First Player takes the first turn and turns proceed clockwise; a Revealed player is skipped for the rest of Player Turns. The phase ends when all players have Revealed. In Combat Intrigue, First Player has first priority and play proceeds clockwise; an eligible player may play any number of Combat Intrigues before passing.
answers.evidence: Player Turns order/ending; Combat: “starting with First Player and continuing clockwise”; “any number”; earlier pass does not bind.

answers.answer: Reveal steps are: reveal all remaining hand cards; resolve their Reveal effects (in any order, with Persuasion purchases before/between/after); Clean Up by moving all in-play cards to discard. Reveal effects need not follow card order.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn three enumerated steps; “in any order.”

answers.answer: Shuffle each human’s 10-card starting deck and put it face down to the left of the Leader. Omit CHOAM-marked cards without the module; shuffle the Intrigue and Imperium decks separately face down, deal five Imperium cards face up as the Row, and place Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow in separate Reserve stacks. The human Combat marker starts at 0; three Spies and the Councilor start in supply; Control markers start in supply.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 4 and 6; personal deck setup; “Place your remaining components (including your 3 Spies) in your supply”; Control markers are player components.

answers.answer: During a Reveal turn, ordinary Persuasion purchases may be any of the five Imperium Row cards, Prepare the Way, or The Spice Must Flow. The acquisition cost is printed at the card’s top right. These purchases happen during Reveal, not an Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: “During your Reveal turn”; cards and costs “shown at the card’s top right.”

answers.answer: Yes. Ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy actions are optional even when a legal choice exists. The Shield Wall detonation icon is also optional. Once removed, the Wall is gone for the rest of the game and cannot return.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: “Ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional”; Shield Wall: “may remove”; “gone for rest of game.”

answers.answer: Ordinarily the played card must show an Agent icon matching the destination. A Spy connected to Shipping does not let a card with only City access visit Shipping. If the card has the Spy Agent icon, the connected Spy permits the Agent to go to any space connected to a post where you have that Spy, without recalling it.
answers.evidence: Agent turn and Spies rules: normal matching icon required; Spy Agent icon grants connected space access.

answers.answer: Yes. On an Agent turn, you may first play a legal Plot Intrigue; resources it grants before Agent placement can pay the destination cost. Resources from the card used to send the Agent or the destination are gained only after placement, so cannot pay that same cost.
answers.evidence: Plot may be played “before placing your Agent”; its grants “can also pay that cost”; gains “only after placement … cannot pay.”

answers.answer: No. In two-player play, after both humans Reveal, continue the Rival’s Agent turns while it has an Agent in supply. Move to Combat only after both humans have Revealed and the Rival has used all its Agents. The Rival never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Player Turns two-player rule.

answers.answer: When a Conflict is revealed for a location the human already controls, they may deploy one troop from supply directly to that Conflict, without an Agent visit; taking the bonus is optional. After rewards, all Combat markers reset to 0 before Makers.
answers.evidence: Round Start defensive bonus; Combat cleanup: “all Combat markers reset to 0.”

answers.answer: Take one card from your hand and play it face up in front of you; send one Agent from your Leader to an unoccupied matching space. Resolve that card’s Agent box, not its Reveal box. You cannot reuse a card already in play or in discard, nor simply move an Agent already on the board; each Agent turn uses a card from hand and an Agent from your Leader.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: “Play one card from your hand face up”; Agent “from your Leader”; “ignore its Reveal box.”

answers.answer: The restriction applies immediately when Shaddam plays Signet Ring to send the Agent. He cannot resolve board effects first to deploy units before it begins; he cannot deploy units to the Conflict for the entire turn.
answers.evidence: Shaddam clarification: restriction “takes effect immediately”; “general freedom to order … effects cannot postpone it”; module says “for that entire turn.”

answers.answer: The first-, second-, and third-highest players each receive the corresponding printed reward; fourth place receives no reward. The highest-strength player wins and takes the Conflict card face up, then checks it for a mandatory battle-icon match.
answers.evidence: Four-player ordinary first, second, third may receive rewards; winner card procedure.

answers.answer: Players may choose their Leaders or select them at random; random distribution is not required.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Each player takes a Leader (choose, or select at random).”

answers.answer: An ordinary draw-a-card effect draws from your own deck, reshuffling your discard pile into a new deck if needed. You may not choose a card directly from your discard pile instead.
answers.evidence: “ordinary draw-a-card effect draws from your own deck”; if empty, shuffle discard and continue.

answers.answer: Shuffle the House Hagal deck and place it near the shared Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card.
answers.evidence: Rival Setup: “Shuffle House Hagal and place the deck near the shared Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card.”

answers.answer: All four Maker Hooks begin in the common bank; normal setup assigns none to a human player. When acquired, a token moves from the bank onto that player’s garrison.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7: “Put all 4 Maker Hooks tokens in this common bank; normal setup assigns none”; later “moves from the bank onto that player’s garrison.”

answers.answer: Yes. If a Combat Intrigue changes deployed units or otherwise alters strength, adjust the participant’s Combat marker when that card resolves during the Combat Intrigue window. Rewards use the adjusted strength shown on the track, not a fixed Reveal value.
answers.evidence: Combat: “adjust their Combat marker when that card resolves”; resolve using “adjusted strength shown on the track.”

answers.answer: Gained Solari, spice, and water come from the common bank; you may not take them from another player’s supply. Payments of these resources go back to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup: “whenever you gain … take it from the bank; whenever you pay … return it to the bank.”

answers.answer: Shuffle the 20 standard contract tokens face down before exposing two face-up offers; put the rest face down in the bank. Players do not choose the offers or preset the order; the summary specifies shuffling, with no selection step.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup: “Shuffle … face down, then flip two face up … put the rest face down in the bank.”

answers.answer: If Shaddam is chosen, first set aside both Sardaukar contracts before shuffling; only Shaddam may acquire them, and he does not start with them. Shuffle the remaining 18 standard contracts, expose 2 as public offers, and put 16 face down in the bank, in addition to the 2 reserved contracts.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup: “first set aside both Sardaukar”; “18 not set aside: two offers and 16 in the bank”; reserved contracts “do not begin in his possession”; only Shaddam may acquire.
